teaser.text: Cencora is a healthcare middleman: it moves medicines from manufacturers to the pharmacies, hospitals, clinics and practices that put them in patients’ hands. It earns money by selling those products and by charging for the logistics, data and practice support that make them easier to use.

stock.opening: Cencora's weighted forecast puts the share price at $351.97 in October 2027 and $411.05 in October 2029. It hinges on earnings growth, specialty acquisition returns, cash conversion and the valuation multiple.
stock.closing: The full memo also examines Cencora's business, rivals, management and risks.

blocks.heading: Where could Cencora's shares be by 2029?

paragraphs.text: The weighted forecast puts the share price at $351.97 in October 2027, a 4% return including dividends. It reaches $411.05 in October 2029, a 23% return including dividends. Bear probability is 25%. Base probability is 55%. Bull probability is 20%.

blocks.heading: What has to go right or wrong for Cencora?

paragraphs.text: The bear case gives earnings of $2,850 million and $3,000 million in the first two windows, then $3,100 million. Its margins stay near 0.83% to 0.84% because of weaker volumes, customer pressure and financing costs. The bull case reaches $4,100 million and $4,600 million before $5,100 million, requiring specialty growth and better mix to lift margins toward 1.19%. The evidence supports progress: FY2025 revenue grew 9.3%, and the latest quarter showed adjusted operating income growth of 17.0%. But GLP-1 sales have modest profitability, and customer concentration remains high.

The bear case requires slower GLP-1 growth, customer losses or repricing, and acquired businesses that add revenue without covering financing and integration costs. By October 2027 it produces $225.36, falling to $215.97 by October 2029. The 25% probability reflects thin margins, concentrated customers, debt and working-capital demands, although the adjusted earnings record and current operating guidance make sustained downside less likely than base progress.

blocks.heading: How much cash does Cencora really make?

paragraphs.text: Cash from operations is cash produced before capital spending. Free cash flow subtracts spending on warehouses, equipment and technology. “Real” free cash flow goes further by subtracting stock-based compensation, because issuing shares still dilutes owners even when it does not immediately use cash.

blocks.heading: What does an investor pay for Cencora today?

paragraphs.text: The price-to-earnings ratio, or P/E, shows what investors pay for each dollar of annual earnings. Cencora’s trailing P/E is much higher than its next-twelve-month P/E, which means the market expects earnings to rise. But fiscal Q2 2026 GAAP diluted earnings per share were $8.40, compared with $4.75 on an adjusted basis. GAAP includes a $1.1 billion OneOncology remeasurement gain; adjusted earnings remove it. The adjusted figure better shows the operating trend, though acquisition and legal costs still deserve scrutiny.

dividend.opening: Cencora pays a dividend per share that has risen every year in the supplied history. Its free cash flow has covered the dividend comfortably, while buybacks can compete with acquisition-debt repayment for the same cash.
dividend.closing: The full memo also answers how Cencora's business works, who its rivals are, how management allocates capital, and what risks could change the outcome.

blocks.heading: How much does Cencora pay per share?

paragraphs.text: The base dividend rises from $2.64 per share to $2.90 and then $3.19. The bear case holds the current $2.40 annual pace before reaching $2.52, while the bull case reaches $2.64, $2.98 and $3.34. The base dividend path receives 65% probability because the dividend has risen every year in the supplied history and free cash flow has covered it comfortably. Debt, legal payments and capex justify a 15% freeze case; stronger specialty cash generation supports a 20% bull case.

blocks.heading: Is Cencora's dividend covered by its cash?

paragraphs.text: Dividends have been the steadier shareholder commitment, while buybacks vary more sharply. Cencora authorized a $2.0 billion repurchase program in May 2026 and repurchased $1 billion of shares in the June 2026 quarter. Those purchases can lift earnings per share, but the same cash cannot also repay acquisition debt. The central question therefore shifts from whether Cencora can generate cash to whether it is directing enough of it toward the investments that matter most.

paragraphs.text: For the year to September 2026, management guides to revenue growth of 4–6% and adjusted operating-income growth of 13–14%. It guides to adjusted diluted EPS of $17.75–$17.95 and adjusted free cash flow of $3.0 billion. Capital expenditures are guided to $900 million.

The November earnings call should bring FY2027 guidance. The case turns on operating income growing faster than revenue, plus the effect of acquisition financing and share count on EPS. A mid-fiscal-year close of the pending MWI Animal Health–Covetrus merger would create a $150 million operating-income headwind and an estimated negative EPS effect of about $0.35; timing remains under regulatory review. Cencora estimated $396.2 million of opioid payments before June 30, 2027.

blocks.heading: What is Cencora's dividend yield today?

paragraphs.text: At $340.92, Cencora trades at 25.3x trailing and 17.3x next-twelve-month earnings. Free cash flow yield is 4.9%, real free cash flow yield is 4.7%, and dividend yield is 0.7%. Revenue grew 9.3% in FY2025, but operating margin was 0.8%. Diluted EPS rose from $7.39 in FY2021 to $7.96 in FY2025, after peaking at $8.53 in FY2023.

blocks.heading: Did Cencora keep its past promises?

paragraphs.text: The fiscal 2025 target deserves scrutiny. Cencora set adjusted free cash flow at $2.0 billion, compared with $3.1 billion in fiscal 2024, citing lost business and investment in distribution centers. Free cash flow then reached the plan’s maximum payout level. The compensation committee reduced the calculated payout from 185.3% to 181.3% after citing underperformance in part of International Healthcare Solutions. It applied discretion, but the lower hurdle still matters.

blocks.heading: What has Cencora's revenue and profit trend been?

paragraphs.text: The June 2026 quarter was operationally strong, but accounting events make the improvement less clean than the headline suggests.

U.S. growth came from unit volume, specialty products and GLP-1 demand. Manufacturer price declines, the loss of an oncology customer and lower sales to a large mail-order customer offset part of that strength. International performance improved, led by European distribution and global specialty logistics. One quarter, however, cannot establish a permanent change in trend.

blocks.heading: What should you watch in Cencora's next results?

paragraphs.text: First, watch the November earnings call. Management said it was still planning fiscal 2027 and would provide full-year guidance then. That outlook should show how operating performance, acquisition interest costs and the expected share count combine in EPS.
